summary: Lavanya V. Eswar is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She was attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar studying at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

Lawrence E. Sullivan is a scholar in religious studies and history and archaeology. He served as Director at Harvard University (attested 2000–2004) and as Professor in the Department of Theology at the University of Notre Dame (attested 2005).

Lawrence Heyworth Mills (1837–1918) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at New York University and held a professorship at the University of Oxford, attested in 1903.

Lawrence J. McCrea is an Indologist, philosopher, and linguist who studied under Sheldon Pollock. He serves as a Professor at Cornell University (attested 2026) and taught Whitney Cox and James McHugh.

Lawrence William Nelson specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy and Religion from the California Institute of Integral Studies, and studied at Butler, Indiana, New York, and Northwestern Universities, among other institutions.
Laxmanshastri Joshi (1901–1994) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Kevalananda Saraswati from circa 1916 to 1923 and served as Director of Prajna Pathashala from circa 1948 to 1994.

Laxmidhar Behera works in computational fields and Indology. He has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur and the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi, and he taught Jivnesh Sandhan.

LeRoy Carr Barret (1877–1960) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Washington and Lee University (~1894–1898) and at Johns Hopkins University (~1899–1903) under Maurice Bloomfield.

Leah Judith Zahler specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981), and also studied under Harvey B. Aronson, Joe Bransford Wilson, and Geshe Wangyal.

Lee Yearley is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and sinology who taught Thomas A. Tweed. He held appointments at Stanford University as Professor (attested 1989–1992) and later as Emeritus (attested 2026).

Leedom Lefferts specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Attested in 2011, he served as Professor of Anthropology, Emeritus, at Drew University and as a Research Associate in the Department of Anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution.

Leela Aditi Wood specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Michigan by 2005 under Luis Oscar Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Leo Frobenius (1873–1938) worked in history and archaeology. He held posts at the Frobenius Institute (1920–1938), Goethe University Frankfurt (1932–1938), and Museum der Weltkulturen (1935–1938), and taught Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf.

Leo M. Pruden (1937–1991) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Taitetsu Unno and at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa, and taught at Brown University, the Nyingma Institute, and the University of Oriental Studies.

Leo Meyer (1830–1910) was a linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey, Jacob Grimm, and Franz Bopp. He held chairs at the University of Tartu (1865–1899) and the University of Göttingen (1862–1865, 1898), teaching Georg Bühler and Leopold von Schroeder.
Leo Rishi Nelson Jones is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg and held a post there as Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter, attested in 2026.

Leo Strauss (1899–1973) was a philosopher who studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, and Marburg. He taught at The New School (~1938–1949) and the University of Chicago (~1949–1969), with later posts at St. John's College and Claremont McKenna College.

Leon Hurvitz (1923–1992) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He served as a professor at the University of Washington (circa 1955–1971) and at the University of British Columbia (circa 1971–1988), continuing there until circa 1992.

Leonard Bloomfield (1887–1949) was a linguist educated at Harvard, Wisconsin, and Chicago under Francis Asbury Wood. He held professorships at Illinois (1910–1921), Ohio State (1921–1927), Chicago (1927–1940), and served as Sterling Professor of Linguistics at Yale (1940–1949).
Leonard Blussé is a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology. He studied at Leiden University from circa 1972 to 1986 and later held an academic post there from 1998 to 2011.
